newsitem.title: USA: Georgia sees post-Olympics loss of 37,000 jobs.
newsitem.headline: Georgia sees post-Olympics loss of 37,000 jobs.

text.p: Georgia lost 37,000 seasonal jobs in August, putting total employment at 3.55 million, state Labor Commissioner David Poythress said Monday.

"The job losses were almost entirely due to the end of the Summer Olympic Games," Poythress said. "Many of the people who worked during the Olympics were from out of state and they have returned to their homes. Others were simply working a part-time summer job during the Olympics."

Restaurants and catering lost 10,000 jobs in August as extra workers hired for the Olympics were laid off. The services sector overall lost 22,200 jobs, mostly at temporary employment agencies that had added workers for the Games, Poythress said.
"Georgia's economy remains strong and payroll employment should increase again in September and continune to grow throught he end of the year," Poythress said.
The state's total employment has risen by 114,200 or 3.3 percent over the year.
With the exception of Savannah, which added 1,000 new jobs in August, most of the job losses came in cities with Olympic venues. Atlanta lost 37,100 jobs, Athens lost 1,400 and Columbus lost 200.
Albany gained 100 jobs, Augusta gained 400 and Macon gained 200.
